'''Detlef Günther''' (born 21 November 1963) is a German-Swiss analytical chemist and professor at [[ETH Zurich]]. He has worked in analytical chemistry, particularly [[mass spectrometry]], [[laser ablation]], and trace-element analysis.<ref name="ETHbio">{{cite web |title=Prof. Detlef Günther |url=https://guenther.ethz.ch/people/prof-detlef-guenther.html |publisher=[[ETH Zurich]] |access-date=22 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260922094644/https://guenther.ethz.ch/people/prof-detlef-guenther.html |archive-date=22 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Günther served as Vice President Research and Corporate Relations at ETH Zurich from 2015 to 2020 and as Vice President Research from 2021 to 2022.<ref name="ETHstepping">{{cite web |title=Stepping down after eight years of dedication to research |url=https://ethz.ch/staffnet/en/news-and-events/internal-news/archive/2022/04/stepping-down-after-eight-years-of-dedication-to-research.html |publisher=[[ETH Zurich]] |date=2022 |access-date=22 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260922122535/https://ethz.ch/staffnet/en/news-and-events/internal-news/archive/2022/04/stepping-down-after-eight-years-of-dedication-to-research.html |archive-date=22 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

He is a member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] and a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref name="Leopoldina">{{cite web |title=Detlef Günther |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/member-list/detail/detlef-guenther |publisher=[[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] |access-date=22 September 2026}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==

Günther was born on 21 November 1963. He attended primary school in Lübs from 1970 to 1978. He attended the Gymnasium in Zerbst, completing his secondary education in 1982. He studied chemistry at [[Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg]], graduating as a ''Diplomchemiker'' in 1987.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Detlef Günther {{!}} Trace Element and Micro Analysis |url=https://whoiswho-umzh.uzh.ch/people/detlef-guenther |access-date=2026-09-22 |website=whoiswho-umzh.uzh.ch |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260922095945/https://whoiswho-umzh.uzh.ch/people/detlef-guenther |archive-date=22 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

He received the degree of ''Dr. rer. nat.'' from the same university in 1990.<ref name="ETHbio"/>

== Career ==

From 1992 to 1994, Günther worked in the Department of Stress Research at the Institute of Plant Biochemistry in Halle in the group of L. Nover.<ref name="ETHbio"/>

In 1994, he moved to the Department of E<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-10-17 |title=“Science is always a discourse” |url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2019/10/interview-detlef-guenther.html |access-date=2026-09-22 |website=ETH Zurich |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260922115246/https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2019/10/interview-detlef-guenther.html |archive-date=22 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> arth Sciences at [[Memorial University of Newfoundland]], where he worked as a postdoctoral researcher with H. P. Longerich.<ref name="ETHbio"/>

From 1995 to 1998, Günther worked in the Department of Isotope Geology and Mineral Resources at ETH Zurich with C. A. Heinrich. During this period, he worked on laser-ablation ICP-MS and its application to geological materials, including fluid inclusions.<ref name="ETHbio"/>

Günther joined ETH Zurich as an assistant professor of analytical chemistry and trace-element analysis in 1998. He became an associate professor and later a full professor. He has headed the Research Group for Elemental and Trace Analysis at ETH Zurich.<ref name="ETHbio"/>

From 1999 to 2003, he chaired the Center of Excellence in Analytical Chemistry at ETH Zurich. He was Head of the Laboratory of Inorganic Chemistry from 2006 to 2008 and chaired the Department of Chemistry and Applied Biosciences from 2010 to 2012.<ref name="ETHcareer">{{cite web |title=Dedicated coach with a passion for research |url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2022/12/dedicated-coach-with-a-passion-for-research.html |publisher=[[ETH Zurich]] |date=2022 |access-date=22 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260922154658/https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2022/12/dedicated-coach-with-a-passion-for-research.html |archive-date=22 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

From 2015 to 2020, Günther served as Vice President Research and Corporate Relations at ETH Zurich. He served as Vice President Research from 2021 to 2022.<ref name="ETHstepping" />

== Research ==

Günther has contributed to the development of [[Laser ablation|laser-ablation]] [[ICP-MS]], including instrumentation for quantitative analysis of geological materials.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-22 |title=Laser-Ablation ICP-MS Imaging of Geological Samples {{!}} Spectroscopy Online |url=https://www.spectroscopyonline.com/view/laser-ablation-icp-ms-imaging-geological-samples |access-date=2026-09-22 |website=www.spectroscopyonline.com |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260922213208/https://www.spectroscopyonline.com/view/laser-ablation-icp-ms-imaging-geological-samples |archive-date=22 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> In 1997, he and colleagues reported the use of a 193&nbsp;nm argon-fluoride excimer laser for laser-ablation ICP-MS microanalysis.<ref name="Günther1997">{{Cite journal |last=GüNther |first=Detlef |last2=Frischknecht |first2=Rolf |last3=Heinrich |first3=Christoph A. |last4=Kahlert |first4=Hans-J. |date=1997 |title=Capabilities of an Argon Fluoride 193 nm Excimer Laser for Laser Ablation Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry Microanalysis of Geological Materials |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/ja/article/12/9/939-944/21538 |journal=J. Anal. At. Spectrom. |language=en |volume=12 |issue=9 |pages=939–944 |doi=10.1039/A701423F |issn=0267-9477|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

His group has investigated aerosol formation and transport during laser ablation, including the effects of carrier gases and particle size on elemental fractionation in LA-ICP-MS.<ref name="GüntherKoch2008">{{Citation |last=Günther |first=Detlef |title=CHAPTER 2: FORMATION OF AEROSOLS GENERATED BY LASER ABLATION AND THEIR IMPACT ON ELEMENTAL FRACTIONATION IN LA–ICP–MS |date=2008 |work=Laser Ablation ICP-MS in the Earth Sciences: Current Practices and Outstanding Issues |pages=19–34 |url=https://doi.org/10.3749/9780921294801.ch02 |access-date=2026-09-22 |publisher=Mineralogical Association of Canada |isbn=978-0-921294-49-8 |last2=Koch |first2=Joachim}}</ref> A 2013 study reported chemical imaging at high spatial resolution using the technique.<ref name="Wang2013">{{Cite journal |last=Wang |first=Hao A. O. |last2=Grolimund |first2=Daniel |last3=Giesen |first3=Charlotte |last4=Borca |first4=Camelia N. |last5=Shaw-Stewart |first5=James R. H. |last6=Bodenmiller |first6=Bernd |last7=Günther |first7=Detlef |date=2013-11-05 |title=Fast Chemical Imaging at High Spatial Resolution by Laser Ablation Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ac400996x |journal=Analytical Chemistry |volume=85 |issue=21 |pages=10107–10116 |doi=10.1021/ac400996x |issn=0003-2700|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 2012, Günther and colleagues reported a portable laser-ablation sampling device designed for elemental analysis of objects outside the laboratory. The system collected laser-generated [[aerosol]]s for laboratory analysis and was developed for applications involving objects that could not readily be transported to a laboratory.<ref name="Glaus2012">{{Cite journal |last=Glaus |first=Reto |last2=Koch |first2=Joachim |last3=Günther |first3=Detlef |date=2012-06-19 |title=Portable Laser Ablation Sampling Device for Elemental Fingerprinting of Objects Outside the Laboratory with Laser Ablation Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ac3008626 |journal=Analytical Chemistry |volume=84 |issue=12 |pages=5358–5364 |doi=10.1021/ac3008626 |issn=0003-2700|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Günther's group has also worked on inductively coupled plasma time-of-flight mass spectrometry (ICP-TOFMS), including applications involving rapidly changing samples and single particles. Research from the group examined the use of ICP-TOFMS for the detection of nanoparticles in microdroplets.<ref name="Gschwind2011">{{Cite journal |last=Gschwind |first=Sabrina |last2=Flamigni |first2=Luca |last3=Koch |first3=Joachim |last4=Borovinskaya |first4=Olga |last5=Groh |first5=Sebastian |last6=Niemax |first6=Kay |last7=Günther |first7=Detlef |date=2011 |title=Capabilities of inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry for the detection of nanoparticles carried by monodisperse microdroplets |url=https://doi.org/10.1039/c0ja00249f |journal=Journal of Analytical Atomic Spectrometry |volume=26 |issue=6 |pages=1166 |doi=10.1039/c0ja00249f |issn=0267-9477|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 2013, the group reported a prototype ICP-TOF mass spectrometer designed for temporally resolved, multi-element detection of short signals generated by individual particles and droplets.<ref name="Borovinskaya2013">{{Cite journal |last=Borovinskaya |first=Olga |last2=Hattendorf |first2=Bodo |last3=Tanner |first3=Martin |last4=Gschwind |first4=Sabrina |last5=Günther |first5=Detlef |date=2013 |title=A prototype of a new inductively coupled plasma time-of-flight mass spectrometer providing temporally resolved, multi-element detection of short signals generated by single particles and droplets |url=https://doi.org/10.1039/c2ja30227f |journal=J. Anal. At. Spectrom. |volume=28 |issue=2 |pages=226–233 |doi=10.1039/c2ja30227f |issn=0267-9477|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 2018, Günther and colleagues reported a nitrogen microwave-induced plasma system as an alternative to argon-based inductively coupled plasma for mass spectrometry.<ref name="Schild2018">{{Cite journal |last=Schild |first=Matthias |last2=Gundlach-Graham |first2=Alexander |last3=Menon |first3=Ashok |last4=Jevtic |first4=Jovan |last5=Pikelja |first5=Velibor |last6=Tanner |first6=Martin |last7=Hattendorf |first7=Bodo |last8=Günther |first8=Detlef |date=2018-11-20 |title=Replacing the Argon ICP: Nitrogen Microwave Inductively Coupled Atmospheric-Pressure Plasma (MICAP) for Mass Spectrometry |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.8b03251 |journal=Analytical Chemistry |volume=90 |issue=22 |pages=13443–13450 |doi=10.1021/acs.analchem.8b03251 |issn=0003-2700|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
